Gosney of Eastleigh beat Olney the local "crack" in the individual race, but our lads packed well with Tom Clinton 4th, Dick Towndrow 5th, Ted Stimpson 6th and Frank Abberton 7th.

Tom Clinton ran a good leg and handed over to George Lucas at Merstham in sixth place. Tom Clinton has also done very well and he won the Portsmouth A.C. 10 miles race on March 29th when we finished second in the team race with Tom Carter 7th and Dick Tobin 11th completing our team.

Newcomers to the team were Tom Clinton, Ken Stimpson, Martin Williamson and Eddie Short. Twenty-five clubs competed in 1949 and we accomplished our second hat-trick of wins, thus achieving more wins in the nineteen races held than any other club.
But Sutton still had five in before our 5th man (Tom Carter 41st) and then praise be, Tommy Clinton came along in 57th place to complete our scoring six, while Sutton's 6th man finished 65th!

Len Herbert had run well throughout as had Ted Stimpson, now getting back to his pre-war form, and with Frank Abberton also making a last lap effort, and Tom Carter and Tommy Clinton coming along well we found to our satisfaction that we had beaten Sutton Harriers, the holders, to record our fourth National victory.

Geoff was one of that rare breed of Belgravian who had sampled team success at the highest level, being fourth scorer, in 21st position, in our winning National Cross Country team at Leamington Spa in 1946. The others in the winning team that day were Len Herbert (5th), Dave Main (11th), Tom Carter (13th), 21 T.G.
